notes: The zip change is minimal and matches the reference, but squashfs New now sets f.file = obj.Remote(), which is computed against the pre-adjustment root. That likely breaks single-file roots nested in a subdirectory for regular files as well as links, and NewObject("dir.rclonelink") can return ErrorNotAFile.

The zip change matches the reference: suffix added before the root check and content read lazily from the member. On the squashfs side, the lookup was restructured into lookupObjectNative/findObjectNative unnecessarily, `f.file = obj.Remote()` (computed before root is moved up a level) risks breaking nested single-file roots, and the link Open does not clamp negative offsets. Tests are good, but the squashfs ones depend on mksquashfs being installed.

Correct for both backends: links are skipped with a notice naming the flag, get the suffix before root matching so a root can name the translated link, and List and NewObject agree. Minor dings are the unused maxLinkTargetSize const in squashfs and eagerly opening every zip symlink at archive-read time, which adds remote reads (e.g. on S3) the reference avoids.

Functionally sound: squashfs newObjectNative matches the suffixed name and reads back the link target, and listing agrees with lookup. However, the zip side eagerly opens and decompresses every symlink member at listing time, an extra cost on S3-backed archives. It also leaves an unused maxLinkTargetSize constant in squashfs and relies on a Readlink assertion on DirEntry that its own (mksquashfs-gated) tests may not exercise.

The main list, lookup and read paths work and the checked-in sqfs testdata exercises them. However, the suffix is applied after root matching, so a root naming `x.rclonelink` is not recognised in either backend, and zip Open special-cases EOF on seek only for links, which looks test-driven.

The core list, NewObject and open path works with lazy zip reads. However, in both backends the suffix is added after root matching, so a root naming the listed `link.txt.rclonelink` is not found while the bare `link.txt` is treated as the link. The squashfs side also silently falls back to an empty target with a mismatched size if StatT is missing, and the zip side special-cases EOF on seek only for links.

Functionally thorough: it handles the root-as-link case and even name collisions between a link and a regular `.rclonelink` file, with strong tests including real sqfs testdata. It does so through a heavy refactor of readZip (zipName/enum/two passes) and a loop in squashfs New that mutates f.root and can map a root `x.rclonelink` onto a regular file `x`.

The most thorough behaviour: it handles name collisions, a root naming the link, and range/seek, and ships committed squashfs testdata plus copy and escape tests. But readZip is heavily refactored (zipName helper, state enum, two passes), symlink targets are read eagerly, and the root lookup loops over candidates while temporarily mutating f.root, which is far more machinery than the task needs.
